extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the NEH Public Scholars Program (2026 Awards for Faculty) preparing book proposals in the humanities
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and review criteria for applying to the NEH Public Scholars grant (Awards for Faculty) to support research and writing of a well‑researched nonfiction humanities book for general readers. Covers eligibility, review criteria, required attachments, formatting, project timeline, and prohibited project types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion 1: Appeal and intellectual significance for general readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal and intellectual significance of the proposed book for general readers, and its potential for promoting a deeper understanding of American history and culture and Western civilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the appeal and significance of the proposed project for general readers; explain why your topic will interest a general audience and how it advances humanities knowledge. Summarize scope and basic ideas, problems, arguments, questions, texts, people, and/or events; discuss relation to previous work and how your work makes a new contribution. (See Narrative: Significance and contribution; narrative limited to 3 pages.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion 2: Applicant’s record and experience in interpreting the humanities for general audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s record of research and experience in interpreting the humanities for general audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain your competence in the project area and describe experience conveying scholarship to broad audiences. If the subject is new, explain reasons and qualifications. Specify language/skill competence, access arrangements to archives or interviews, and collaborators’ competencies. Provide résumé items (positions, education, publications, awards) on resume.pdf (max 2 pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion 3: Quality of conception, definition, organization, and underlying research
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the conception, definition, organization, and description of the project; and the breadth and depth of the humanities research underlying the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss sources and research materials; explain use of primary and/or secondary sources (documents, artifacts, visual works, digital resources, interviews, surveys, fieldwork). Explain how you will locate/select sources and how they support your treatment. Provide a chapter outline and brief chapter explanations in the narrative. Peer reviewers use the bibliography to assess knowledge. (Narrative max 3 pages; Bibliography max 1 page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion 4: Quality of the writing sample and clarity of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality of the writing sample and the applicant’s clarity of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a writing sample that demonstrates how the final product will read and ability to appeal to a general audience—NEH strongly recommends a draft chapter or partial chapter. Sample must be the author's work (unless project is co‑authored). Writing sample must not exceed 20 PDF pages; recommend ~7,000 words; font no smaller than 11‑point; double‑spaced recommended; single‑spaced samples exceeding 20 double‑spaced equivalent may not receive full consideration. Sample may include endnotes/footnotes/tables/visuals within 20 pages. If drawn from proposed book include a headnote explaining relation. Do not include table of contents/outline/abstract in sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review criterion 5: Feasibility of plan, dissemination, and likelihood of completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The feasibility and appropriateness of the proposed plan of work, the soundness and probable reach of the dissemination plan, and the likelihood that the applicant will complete the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a work plan (schedule in increments of three months or fewer) showing current state and tasks during period of performance; include locations and time in each. Explain plans to secure a publisher or dissemination/marketing plans if you have one; if proposing supplemental digital materials, discuss technical specs and maintenance beyond performance period. Work plan must not depend heavily on factors beyond your control (e.g., outside reviewers’ reports). Work plan max 1 page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Publication requirement (must have one nonfiction sole‑authored book)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have written at least one nonfiction book published by a university or trade press and be credited as its sole author. You must list relevant publication(s) on your résumé with identifying citation; NEH will reject proposals that fail to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co‑authored volumes, edited collections/anthologies, scholarly editions, translations, dissertations, unpublished books, or self‑published books (including those where author pays press) do not satisfy this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Residency/citizenship and other NEH awards
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. citizens residing domestically or abroad and foreign nationals who have lived in the United States or its jurisdictions for at least the three years prior to the application deadline are eligible. You may not accept or hold any other NEH individual award in the same federal fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Individual Programs NOFO sections C.1 and C.2 for full eligibility, resubmission, collaborative projects, and projects supported by previous NEH grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited project types / Funding restrictions specific to this program
rubrics_metrics.description: You may not use awards for projects that do not involve research in American history and culture or Western civilization; fiction (including historical fiction and philosophical novels); anthologies and edited collections of essays or primary source documents; publications consisting primarily of transcribed interviews, oral histories, or responses to questionnaires; translations and scholarly editions; projects whose primary product will be a digital archive or database, or audiovisual materials; projects devoted primarily to promoting or disseminating a completed book; development of curricula or teaching methods and theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section A.2 in the Individual Programs NOFO for the full list of funding restrictions for awards to individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of performance constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Scholars awards can be from 6 to 12 months; the period of performance must be continuous and may be part‑time, full‑time, or a combination, but may not be less than the equivalent of six full‑time months nor exceed 12 months. Projects must start between April 1, 2027 and September 1, 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you propose a time period of less than the equivalent of six full‑time months, NEH will reject your application. You must work at least half‑time on your project throughout your period of performance. While holding a full‑time award, forego other major activities including teaching; if working part‑time, carry a reduced teaching load. Period must be continuous even if combining part‑/full‑time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission and deadline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted via Grants.gov and be complete, follow length and formatting requirements, and be validated under the correct funding opportunity prior to the deadline to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application Deadline: April 22, 2026, 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time. Follow instructions in the Individual Programs NOFO and apply under the correct funding opportunity number (20260422‑FZ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment and file format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments must be PDFs and conform to formatting requirements: pages no larger than standard letter size (8½" x 11"), margins of at least one inch on all sides, single‑spacing, readable font (Arial, Georgia, Helvetica, or Times New Roman) no smaller than 11 points. Any standard citation style is acceptable; citations are included in page count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name attachment files as specified (e.g., narrative.pdf, workplan.pdf, bibliography.pdf, resume.pdf, writingsample.pdf, publisherletter.pdf, delinquentdebt.pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 1 — Narrative: organization, content, and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative (narrative.pdf) is required and must not exceed three pages. Organize the narrative using headings: a. Significance and contribution; b. Sources and organization; c. Competencies, skills, and access; d. Final product and dissemination. Each section aligns with one or more review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative should be succinct, well organized, free of technical jargon so peer reviewers can understand. Per NEH AI policy, acknowledge (by footnote or marginal notation) any AI‑generated text inserted into your proposal. Include chapter outline and brief explanations of each chapter’s contents in the narrative (not in the work plan).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 2 — Work plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Work plan (workplan.pdf) is required and must not exceed one page. Present a schedule for the period of performance in increments of three months or fewer, in narrative or table form. Indicate current state of the project and tasks to accomplish during the performance period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include a chapter outline (chapter outlines belong in the narrative). The work plan should not depend heavily on factors beyond your control (e.g., receipt of outside reviewers’ reports from a publisher). Include locations where you will work and time at each. If prior NEH support exists, indicate program and accomplishments and how proposed plan builds on previous support. If collaborating, explain division of work and dependencies. Name file workplan.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 3 — Bibliography requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliography (bibliography.pdf) is required and must not exceed one page. It should consist of primary and secondary sources that relate directly to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include works that pertain to both the project's substance and its theoretical or methodological approaches to give a well‑rounded representation. Peer reviewers will use the bibliography to assess your knowledge of the subject area. Any standard bibliographic format is acceptable. Items referenced in the narrative need not appear in the bibliography if the citation in the narrative enables identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 4 — Résumé requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Résumé (resume.pdf) is required and must not exceed two pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include current and past positions; education with degrees/dates/titles of theses or dissertations; awards and honors with dates (indicate prior NEH support and resulting products); publications with full citations; other relevant professional activities and accomplishments; level of competence in digital tools/methodologies and relevant foreign languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 5 — Writing sample requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing sample (writingsample.pdf) is required and must not exceed 20 PDF pages. NEH strongly recommends a draft chapter or partial chapter of the proposed book; if unavailable, a sample in the style of the proposed book is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample should demonstrate how the final product will read and ability to appeal to a general audience. If typescript, use font no smaller than 11‑point and NEH recommends double‑spacing; single‑spaced samples containing more than the equivalent of 20 double‑spaced pages may not receive full consideration. May include endnotes/footnotes/tables/visuals/captions/bibliography/headnote within 20‑page limit. If reproducing previously published pages you may include one or two published pages per PDF page and may abridge with a note. If sample is from proposed book include a headnote explaining how it relates (which chapter, complete/partial). The sample may not include table of contents, outline, or abstract. You must be the author of the sample unless proposing a co‑authored book. NEH recommends submitting a single piece rather than multiple pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 6 — Publisher’s letter of interest or commitment (optional) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional letter from an official representative of a publisher indicating planning/exploration of publication arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of commitment should indicate physical format(s) planned for the book, dissemination plans, and print‑run expectations. If submitted, the letter must be included with other materials at time of application and may not be added after the deadline. Name file publisherletter.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 7 — Explanation of delinquent federal debt (conditionally required)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive an offer of an award and are delinquent on federal debt, you will be asked to provide explanatory information and evidence of a repayment agreement and current status; NEH encourages submission with the application but will require it if you receive an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of relevant debt include delinquent student loans, taxes, child support, and payroll taxes for household or other employees. See OMB Circular A‑129. Name file delinquentdebt.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of reference submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of reference must be submitted online no later than May 6, 2026, to ensure full consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 4: Letters of Reference in the Individual Programs NOFO for additional information on content and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application component table / required attachments mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete application must include specified Grants.gov forms and attachments with required file names and page limits: Narrative (3 pages), Work plan (1 page), Bibliography (1 page), Résumé (2 pages), Writing sample (20 pages), Publisher’s letter (optional), Explanation of delinquent federal debt (conditionally required), plus SF‑424, NEH Supplemental Information for Individuals Form, Project/Performance Site(s) Location Form, and Attachments Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure attachments conform to the required filenames (narrative.pdf, workplan.pdf, bibliography.pdf, resume.pdf, writingsample.pdf, publisherletter.pdf, delinquentdebt.pdf) and that all Grants.gov forms are completed as instructed in the Individual Programs NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI disclosure policy for NEH proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Per the Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence for NEH Grant Proposals, you must acknowledge (by use of footnotes or other marginal notations) when you have inserted AI‑generated text into your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include acknowledgements within the proposal documents (e.g., narrative) where AI content is present; follow whatever brief notation format is used consistently so reviewers can identify AI‑generated text.
